items.title: Magistrate can take cognisance of private complaint only after examining complainant and hearing the accused: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Tuesday ruled that in a private complaint, the magistrate court can take cognisance of an offence only after examining the complainant and the witnesses on oath and giving an opportunity of hearing to the accused. A Division Bench of Justices Navin Chawla and Ravinder Dudeja said that under Section 223(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), the examination of the complainant and the witnesses and hearing the accused are steps prior to taking cognisance of the offence. In a detailed order, the Court also answered the question as to what stage the magistrate is required to issue notice to the accused in compliance with the first proviso to Section 223(1) of the BNSS. “The Magistrate is required to issue a notice to the accused, in compliance with the first proviso to Section 223(1) of the BNSS, after examining the complainant and the witnesses present on oath, unless exempted, and forming a prima facie opinion that the complaint does not deserve to be dismissed under Section 226 of the BNSS but cognizance may deserve to be taken of the offence,” it said. Justice Navin Chawla and Justice Ravinder Dudeja The Court returned these findings while deciding references arising from two petitions. The Division Bench was called upon to settle the stage at which cognisance is taken in a private complaint under the BNSS and when notice must be issued to the proposed accused. After considering the arguments, the Court said that unlike Section 200 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), Section 223 BNSS provides that no cognisance can be taken without giving the accused an opportunity of being heard. It held that the examination of the complainant and witnesses is part of the process leading to cognisance, rather than a step occurring after cognisance as under the CrPC. The court also rejected the argument that magistrates should have discretion to issue notice either before or after recording the complainant’s statement. It held that where examination is statutorily required, notice would ordinarily have greater meaning after the statements have been recorded, enabling the proposed accused to make an effective representation. “The legislature clearly wanted to divert from the earlier position under the CrPC where the accused did not have a right to be heard at that stage, and faced a prolonged trial which was bound to fail. items.summary: The Supreme Court has sought a formal explanation from its registry regarding the unceremonious deletion of a batch of contempt of court petitions concerning the deputation of 46 Indian Police Service (IPS) officers to Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) [ Mahendra Singh Deo v. Govind Mohan ]. In an order passed on Tuesday, a Bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and AS Chandurkar noted that the matter had been deleted from the afternoon roster during the lunch recess, despite standing judicial orders mandating its listing at 2:00 PM. "The Court has been informed at 2 pm that the case has been struck off from the cause list during the lunch break. items.title: Karnataka High Court stays forgery case against cult.fit co-founder Rishabh Telang
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on September 28 stayed the investigation in criminal proceedings initiated against fitness platform Cult.fit's co-founder Rishabh Telang on allegations of cheating, forgery and criminal breach of trust, among others [Rishabh Telang v. State of Karnataka]. Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde granted the interim stay on investigation and will hear the matter on September 30. "Since the matter is heard on merits, further investigation is stayed till the next date of hearing." Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde The case stemmed from a complaint filed by Telang’s brother-in-law and Cult co-founder Deepak Poduval accusing him of forging documents connected to the transfer of the original Cult business and the subsequent closure of Cult Fitness Private Limited. Bellandur Police lodged an FIR against Telang on August 6. Poduval alleged that he and Telang incorporated Cult Fitness in November 2015 as its only two subscribers, with each holding a 50 per cent stake. According to the complaint, Telang subsequently excluded him from the management of the company and diverted its business, customers, goodwill and revenue to Cultfit Healthcare Private Limited, which was incorporated in August 2016. Poduval further alleged that his signatures were forged on financial statements and documents submitted to the Registrar of Companies to have Cult Fitness struck off in 2019. He claimed that he discovered the alleged irregularities only after examining the company’s records in May and June 2026. The FIR invoked provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita concerning criminal breach of trust, cheating, forgery, use of forged documents and criminal conspiracy, along with Section 66D of the Information Technology Act. Senior Advocate Sandesh Chouta , appearing for Telang, submitted the dispute is a commercial in nature and that criminal proceedings have been initiated to harass his client. Senior Advocate Sandesh J Chouta Chouta was assisted by Advocates Mohammed Shakeeb, Chetan Tayal and Sathies Kumar from Multi State Collaborative Legal. Advocate Ahaan Mohan appeared for Poduval. items.title: Ten years on, still struggling to execute foreign arbitral award: Daiichi tells Supreme Court
items.summary: Japanese pharmaceutical company Daiichi Sankyo told the Supreme Court on Tuesday that nearly ten years after securing a foreign arbitral award against former Ranbaxy promoters Malvinder Mohan Singh and Shivinder Mohan Singh, it was still struggling to execute the award [Yes Bank Vs Daiichi Sankyo]. Senior Advocate Arvind Datar , appearing for Daiichi, said the company had pursued arbitration, obtained an award on April 29, 2016 and then initiated execution proceedings, but was yet to realise the award. " It’s 10 years to execute an award, international award ,” Datar said. He added that the situation has become a “spider’s web”, with disputes continuing over what happened to shares of Fortis Healthcare Limited (FHL) held by the judgment debtors. Supreme Court, Arvind Datar The submissions were made before a Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana during the hearing of challenges by banks and financial institutions to the Delhi High Court’s directions for a forensic audit in the execution proceedings initiated by Daiichi. Datar told the Court that the banks and the judgment debtors have taken conflicting stands on whether certain Fortis shares were encumbered, who invoked the pledges and who ultimately sold the shares. “The banks blame the judgment-debtors, judgment-debtors blame the bank, and I am the decree-holder, I am not getting any relief at all, ” he submitted. Datar also explained why Daiichi had earlier stated that it did not want to pursue a forensic audit against the banks. He said there were 17 banks involved and that Daiichi had taken the stand out of “sheer frustration”, since hearing every bank separately would further prolong the execution proceedings. Daiichi had therefore asked that the forensic exercise proceed “once and for all”. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, CJI Surya Kant and Justice V Mohana The banks, on the other hand, argued that they were neither judgment debtors nor garnishees and that some of them were themselves owed money by the judgment debtors or their group entities. Senior Advocate Shyam Divan argued that opening up the books of a bank to a third-party forensic auditor would have serious consequences, particularly when Daiichi itself had ultimately said that it did not want a forensic audit of the banks. items.title: UDF setback as LDF wrests seven wards in Keralam local body bypolls
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) suffered a setback in Keralam’s local body bye-elections, with the Left Democratic Front (LDF) wresting seven wards from it. Two of the wards had been vacated by sitting UDF MLAs. The UDF won 19 of the 38 wards, while the opposition LDF won 18. Twenty20, an ally of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA), won the remaining seat. Before the bye-elections, the UDF held 22 of the wards, the LDF 15, and the NDA one. Bye-elections were held across 38 local body wards in 12 districts of Keralam, excluding Kollam and Alappuzha. The results mark the first major electoral test for the VD Satheesan-led UDF government. The UDF retained key wards including the Ayyappankkavu division in the Kochi Corporation and Kuttichira in the Kozhikode Corporation. However, its margin in Kuttichira was lower than in the previous election. The LDF’s gains included seven wards wrested from the UDF across districts including Kannur, Kottayam, Palakkad, and Thiruvananthapuram. The seats captured by the LDF include the the Thrikkodithanam Division of the Kottayam District Panchayat, previously held by sitting Changanassery MLA Vinu Job Kuzhimanmil, and the Paruthikkavu Division in Chittur-Thathamangalam Municipality, held by Chittur MLA Sumeesh Achuthan. The LDF also retained the district panchayat seat held by Left-backed MLA T M Shashi, increasing its majority. Twenty20 retained the Kolenchery East ward in Puthencruz panchayat in Ernakulam, giving the NDA its lone seat in the bye-elections. The BJP did not win any ward. The State Election Commission recorded an overall voter turnout of 58.81%, with 3,09,713 voters casting their ballots.

The Ibrahimpatnam police in Andhra Pradesh’s NTR district arrested a 35-year-old man on Sunday, September 27, for allegedly killing a 30-year-old woman, dismembering her body, and dumping the remains in a cooling canal leading to the Narla Tatarao Thermal Power Station (NTTPS). The accused has been identified as Mohammed Shafi, a resident of Vijayawada’s Bhavanipuram, who allegedly killed Valluripalli Kalyani, a native of Tadinada village in Eluru district who was staying in Mangalagiri, near Vijayawada. A second accused, Durga Rao alias Abdullah, who allegedly helped Shafi dismember and dispose of the body, is absconding. The case came to light on September 18 when police received information about the torso of an unidentified person lying near the VTPS cooling canal. With the assistance of a National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) team, police searched the canal and subsequently recovered the victim’s remains. The remains were sent to Vijayawada government hospital for postmortem examination. Police circulated details and photographs of the unidentified body through social media and other channels, following which Kalyani’s brother approached the police after recognising a tattoo on her hand. According to Vijayawada (West) Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Durga Rao, Kalyani had given birth to a son a few years ago while in a relationship with another man. While the relationship did not culminate in a marriage, Shafi, who already had three daughters and wished for a son, agreed to adopt the child, he said. According to the ACP, the police found that whenever Kalyani was in need of money, she borrowed from Shafi. “She told Shafi that he either give her more money or return the child back to her. Shafi was attached to his adopted son. He decided to put an end to the harassment by murdering Kalyani,” he added. items.title: Four Telangana men allegedly sent to Russian frontline after being promised jobs
items.summary: Four men from the erstwhile Nizamabad district in Telangana, who travelled to Russia in search of employment, are reportedly stranded in the war zone after allegedly being recruited into the Russian military. Their families have approached the Telangana government seeking intervention to ensure their safe return. The four men have been identified as Bhookya Ravinder, 44, from Nallagutta Thanda in Munipally, Jakranpally; Sirshu Ashok, 44, from Oddera Colony in Sirikonda; Megavath Prakash, 40, from Cheruvu Thanda in Dammannapet village of Dharpally; and Mohammed Afzal Khan, 43, from Tadkole in Banswada, Kamareddy district. According to their families, the men travelled to Russia after being promised jobs in the oil industry. However, they allegedly did not receive their salaries and were subsequently persuaded to take up alternative work that resulted in them being sent to a military camp. The families alleged that an agent, Thelu Krishna from Domakonda mandal in Kamareddy district, who is based in Russia, had promised the men that they would work in military support services and would not be involved in combat. They were allegedly later trained to handle weapons and ammunition and deployed to the frontline in Russian-occupied areas of Ukraine. Sirushu Saritha, Ashok’s wife, said her husband travelled to Russia in February after an agent from Isaipet village in Machareddy mandal promised him a job with an oil company. “He was not paid his salary even after two months. He and three others were subsequently lured into the Russian military,” she was quoted as saying by The Hindu . Saritha said the family had been trying to secure her husband’s return. She recently married off their elder daughter while Ashok was still in Russia. Mohammed Afzal Khan’s wife, Jameela Begum, said the family had been under severe emotional strain after receiving distress messages from him. “Ever since we heard his voice messages, neither I nor my in-laws and other family members have been able to sleep,” she told The Times of India . Afzal Khan’s father, Abbas Khan, said his son left for Russia on February 15. He has a son, a daughter, and a wife with a disability. Ravinder’s family said his two sons, Nithin and Arvind, are dependent on him. items.title: Keralam: IDSFFK filmmakers demand jury screening of films withheld by Union govt
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. More than 50 filmmakers whose works were selected for the International Documentary and Short Film Festival of Kerala (IDSFFK) have signed a statement urging the Kerala Chalachitra Academy to screen all the films in competition for the jury, or else cancel the competition and award no one. The statement comes after repeated requests to the Academy to screen all the films selected for the festival failed, following the Union government’s objection to some of them without giving any reason. Filmmakers whose works have been allowed to screen at the festival have also joined the cause, along with hundreds of delegates. The sentiment of the filmmakers is echoed in a letter that jury members from the last two years of the festival have written to the chairperson of the Academy, Ravindran. “We are deeply disturbed to learn that 7 films were removed from the festival programming line-up because the Ministry of I&B arbitrarily withheld permission for their public screenings, without giving any specific reasons whatsoever. We are particularly dismayed to learn that IDSFFK administration has decided not to let the Jury see the following 5 of these films selected for Competition,” began the letter, written by former jury members including Rakesh Sharma, who won the Lifetime Achievement Award for his documentaries at the IDSFFK in 2025. Initially, the Union Ministry of Information and Broadcasting had denied permission for 31 films . However, after the Kerala government’s intervention, permission was granted to 24 of these, including one on the waiting list. Of the seven films excluded from the list, five are in competition. The makers of these films have since been urging the Academy to at least allow a screening for the jury so the competition can be conducted fairly. However, even after the jury agreed to watch the films, the Academy has not allowed it. The Academy had taken the matter to court, with a plea to allow the screening. However, the court adjourned the hearing to November 13. The festival, being held from September 25 to 30, has therefore proceeded without the five films being screened for the jury. Following this, the filmmakers staged a protest outside the Kairali Theatre complex on the evening of September 28. items.title: Telangana HC directs DGP to identify cops accused of manhandling BRS women MLAs
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The Telangana High Court on Tuesday, September 29, directed Director General of Police (DGP) CV Anand to identify police personnel allegedly involved in misbehaving with or manhandling women legislators of the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS). The alleged manhandling took place during a confrontation at the Assembly gates earlier this month. The DGP has been directed to submit details of the personnel to Speaker Gaddam Prasad Kumar for appropriate action. If the alleged incident took place outside the Assembly precincts, including at the entry gate, the DGP has been asked to report the matter to the court. Justice T Madhavi Devi had, on September 7, originally directed authorities not to prevent legislators from attending House proceedings, noting that enforcing internal rules or decorum falls solely within the Speaker's domain and not the police's. While the court declined to cancel the core interim protection allowing MLAs to enter the Assembly on September 29, it modified the directions concerning police conduct and asked the DGP to probe the matter. The case stems from a chaotic start to the monsoon session, when BRS MLAs wearing black T-shirts and shouting anti-Congress slogans were stopped at the Assembly entrance. The BRS alleged that police personnel manhandled its women members, including former minister Sabitha Indra Reddy and MLA Sunitha Lakshma Reddy. The allegations became a central part of the party's petition before the court. The High Court also questioned several aspects of the state's defence. It noted that a September 7 communication from the Legislature Secretary, cited by the government as authorising police intervention, was not mentioned in its counter-affidavit. The court further pointed out that the FIR was registered at 4 pm, after the communication was issued at 3:30 pm, while the alleged violation of police prohibitory orders was not cited in the FIR. The court said those prohibitory orders concerned assemblies and processions around the Assembly and did not appear to cover legislators entering the House. It also found the police response to the allegations concerning the women MLAs insufficient, noting that there was no material before it showing that the women legislators had misbehaved with the police or violated any direction of the Speaker. items.title: ‘Savukku’ Shankar gets 3-year jail term in defamation case filed by former newsreader
items.summary: YouTuber ‘Savukku’ Shankar has been convicted in a defamation case filed by former Sun TV news reader and advocate Mahalakshmi. A Chennai court on Tuesday, September 29, sentenced Shankar to three years in prison and imposed a fine of Rs 20,000. Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Sivashakthi found Shankar guilty under Section 509 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), which deals with words or acts intended to insult the modesty of a woman, and Section 4 of the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act. The court also granted Shankar 30 days to appeal against the verdict. Mahalakshmi had first lodged a complaint against Shankar in 2013, alleging that he had published defamatory remarks about her on his website, ‘Savukku’. She subsequently approached the Egmore court, accusing Shankar and his associates of threatening her, defaming her and fabricating documents. During the proceedings, Mahalakshmi’s lawyer argued that Shankar had deliberately published defamatory allegations against her and issued threats, and sought legal action against him. Shankar’s counsel denied the allegations and argued that the complaints and charges against him were false. After hearing the arguments, the court held that the charges against Shankar under the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act had been proved and sentenced him to three years’ imprisonment. 'Savukku' Shankar is a former government employee who was suspended from the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption. He currently runs a YouTube channel ‘Savukku Media’, where he makes controversial videos often criticising politicians, bureaucrats and the judiciary too, leading to defamation cases against him. The previous DMK government had detained Shankar under the stringent Goondas Act and prolonged his incarceration. However, the newly-formed TVK government revoked the Act against him and ensured his release from prison.
